summary: Overall quality is high. Every numeric key, worked example and table value in all 14 units was recomputed independently in Python (spindle speed and feed, scallop height s^2/(8R), takt, line balancing, Little's law, kanban, OEE-free lean arithmetic, unit cost and break-even, GUM budgets, Xbar-R constants for n=5, Cp/Cpk and normal tails, binomial and hypergeometric acceptance probabilities). All keys and tolerances matched, and the G-code, arc direction, 3-2-1 and ISO 9001:2015 statements are correct. Two major issues were found, one wrong marking-guide fact in the takt unit and one misleading 'all shafts are good' claim in the control-chart unit, plus a handful of minor clarity and scope points. Not covered in this course (not in the stated objectives, so not flagged as errors): OEE, SMED, 8D, cost of quality, p and c charts, Pp/Ppk, AOQ, position tolerance and bonus tolerance. This is an AI review only; the course still needs a subject-matter expert before engineering reliance.

issues.problem: Marking guide says 'stations at 55 s and 60 s now exceed it' for a 48 s takt with stations 55, 60, 50 and 25 s. The 50 s station also exceeds 48 s, so three of the four stations are bottlenecks. The guide's explanation repeats the omission.
issues.suggestedFix: State that the 55, 60 and 50 s stations all exceed the 48 s takt (only the 25 s station is within it). Add this to the marking guide and the explanation.

issues.problem: Hook: 'The latest five average 25.033 mm: still inside the tolerance, so every shaft is good'. Warning callout: 'Control charts signal the change while all parts are still good'. A subgroup mean inside the tolerance does not mean every shaft is. With the lesson's own sigma-hat of 0.0138 mm and a mean of 25.033, about 11% of shafts exceed the USL of 25.05 (z about 1.24). Even at the old mean of 25.012, about 0.3% are already out.
issues.suggestedFix: Reword to 'the average is still inside the tolerance, yet the process has shifted and parts will soon go out of tolerance'. In the callout say the chart warns before the reject rate becomes serious, not while all parts are good. Alternatively use a smaller sigma or a smaller shift so the claim holds.

issues.problem: Distractor d) 'Two machines are needed because utilisation is 58%' has a correct conclusion (two machines are needed; the explanation says each would run at about 59%) with a faulty reason, so it is partly right. The 58% versus 59% figures also disagree (57600 s available, two machines give 58.6%).
issues.suggestedFix: Make d) clearly wrong, for example 'Two machines are not needed because 45 s is under a minute'. Use 59% consistently if the 58.6% figure is kept.

issues.problem: The bullet says to leave margin below 100% (many plants aim for 80 to 90%), while the warning callout says 'Running the bottleneck at 100% is desirable'. These pull in opposite directions for a student.
issues.suggestedFix: Rephrase the callout: the bottleneck should be kept busy, but planning to 100% planned utilisation leaves no slack for variation.

issues.problem: The profile worked example says to 'write the cutting blocks' but shows no Z plunge or feed to depth, no spindle start, and no mention that the programmed path is the tool-centre path (cutter radius compensation or an offset is needed to cut the stated outline). The hook mentions a plunge and a seven-line program.
issues.suggestedFix: Add one line stating the blocks assume the Z depth is already set and the path is the tool-centre path (or add G01 Z- and an offset note).

issues.problem: The key 0.08 mm is correct (0.10/1.25), but the explanation never shows the calculation. Option a) is worded 'the same feed rate is spread over more teeth passes', which is not a precise reason.
issues.suggestedFix: State f_z = F/(zN), so f_z new = 0.10/1.25 = 0.08 mm, and reword option a) to 'because chip thickness is inversely proportional to spindle speed at constant F'.

issues.problem: The unit title is 'Time Standards and Costing', but no time standard content (normal time, allowances, standard time, time study) is taught. Only machining-time formulas and costing appear.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename to 'Machining Time and Costing', or add a short standard-time section.

issues.problem: The mcq keys of q005, q006, q007 and q008 are all option a) (the four mcq in the unit), so the answer position is predictable. The sibling unit also has 4 of 5 keys on a).
issues.suggestedFix: Shuffle option order so the keys are spread over a to d.

issues.problem: The PDCA lesson attributes oversize bores to tool wear, while q002 attributes undersize bores to a worn boring bar. Tool wear on a boring or reaming tool normally gives undersize bores. The lean unit also lists 'Rework of oversize bores', but an oversize bore generally cannot be reworked by re-boring.
issues.suggestedFix: Use undersize bores (or oversize external diameters) caused by tool wear throughout, or name a different cause for oversize bores such as thermal growth or offset drift.

issues.problem: The GUM vocabulary is thin. Type A and Type B evaluation are never named, and the combination formula u_c = sqrt(sum u_i^2) omits sensitivity coefficients c_i (the caption only says 'same unit'). The temperature term is converted to length by hand without saying that this is the coefficient. Triangular distributions (a/sqrt6) are not mentioned. The formulas given are correct as far as they go.
issues.suggestedFix: Add one sentence labelling repeatability as Type A and the rectangular terms as Type B, and state u_c = sqrt(sum (c_i u_i)^2) with c_i = 1 when each term is already in the measurand's unit. Optionally mention triangular u = a/sqrt6.

issues.problem: Marking guide and explanation call a micrometer 'marginal' for a 0.012 mm band (required accuracy 0.0012 mm). The lesson table gives about 0.004 mm accuracy, which is over three times too large, and the lesson's own worked example says the micrometer falls short at a 0.02 mm band.
issues.suggestedFix: Say the micrometer does not meet 10-to-1 for 0.012 mm (4 um against 1.2 um); a comparator with a master or a calibrated high-accuracy CMM is needed.

issues.problem: The unit is titled 'CMM and Geometric Inspection' but has no GD&T content: no position tolerance zones, feature-control frames, or material-condition modifiers (MMC/LMC and bonus tolerance), though the hook quotes a 'position tolerance of 0.04 mm'. The stated objectives (DRF, flatness, traceability) are covered.
issues.suggestedFix: Retitle to 'CMM Inspection and Datum Frames', or add a short position-tolerance section (diameter zone = 2 sqrt(dx^2+dy^2), bonus tolerance only with MMC/LMC).

issues.problem: The lesson uses a single sigma for Cp and Cpk and does not say whether it is the within-subgroup estimate (R-bar/d2) or the overall sample standard deviation. Pp/Ppk are never distinguished. The small-tail values in the worked example are slightly rounded, for example Phi(-2.67)=0.00379, while 0.00383 (z=2.667) is shown. Neither changes any key.
issues.suggestedFix: Add one sentence that Cp/Cpk use the within-subgroup sigma (R-bar/d2) while Pp/Ppk use the overall standard deviation, and quote 0.00383 against z=2.667 or 0.0038 against z=2.67.
